title: How to Spot and Block Fake Bank Text Message Alerts
bigPicture: Fake bank texts try to trick you into giving away your money or passwords, but you can stop them by staying calm and checking before you click.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Banks will never ask for your full password, PIN, or one-time code in a text message.
A real bank text usually has your name or account nickname, not just 'Dear Customer'.
Fake texts often create panic by saying your account is locked or money is missing.
Links in texts can take you to fake websites that steal your login info.
You can block numbers that send you fake texts on your phone.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Clicking links in texts that say your account has a problem.
Replying with personal info like your Social Security number or card code.
Not calling your bank directly when a text feels wrong.
actionSteps: If a text looks fake, do not click any links or call any numbers in the message.
Call your bank using the phone number on the back of your debit card.
Tell your bank about the fake text so they can warn other customers.
Block the sender's number in your phone settings.
Delete the fake text message right away.
